chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father Sayf ibn Umayrah, who said: Al-Hajjaj ibn Artat narrated to me, that Abu al-Zubayr narrated, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said:

The two inevitable outcomes: Whoever dies with testimony that there is no god but Allah (He is One, He has no partner) will enter Paradise, and whoever dies with testimony of associating partners with Allah will enter Hellfire.

key_terms.الْشِّرِكُ: Polytheism or associating partners with God
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (the declaration of monotheism)
key_terms.وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ: He is One, He has no partner (emphasizing divine unity)

ai.seo_question: What are the two inevitable outcomes for a person based on their faith at the time of death?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this hadith emphasizes the decisive role of final faith state (*hal*) in determining eternal destiny, a key concept in Shia eschatology. It underscores that pure monotheism (*Tawhid*) without associating partners with God is the sole criterion for Paradise, while *Shirk* leads inevitably to Hellfire, reflecting the theological weight of divine unity in Shia scholarship.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 8. My father (rh) said, that Sa’d ibn `Abdullah informed us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Sayf, on the authority of his brother Ali, on the authority of his father Sayf ibn Amirah said, that al-Hajjaj ibn Artat related to me, that Abu al-Zubayr said, on the authority of Jabir ibn `Abdullah, from the The Prophet (sw) who said: “

Two events are inevitable: The one who died witnessing that there is no god but Allah (He is One and He has no partner with Him) will enter Paradise, and the one who died associating partners with Allah will enter Hellfire.”
